Geography is a brutal dictator. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. just admitted his country won't have the luxury of sitting out a war over Taiwan, stating plainly that Manila has no choice but to be involved. This is not military bravado. It is a cold, inescapable calculation of survival.

The northernmost Philippine islands sit right on Taiwan's doorstep, meaning any missile exchange or naval blockade will instantly spill into domestic airspace and waters. Furthermore, nearly 200,000 Filipino nationals live and work in Taiwan, creating an immediate humanitarian evacuation nightmare in an active combat zone the moment a conflict begins.

By expanding U.S. military access to strategic bases facing the strait and preparing a tight maritime defense matrix with Japan, Marcos is locking in allied deterrence. Beijing is predictably furious, accusing Manila of playing with fire. But Marcos is just stating a structural fact: when a storm hits the strait, the neighbor’s house gets hit by the debris.

A total of 25 individuals were affected after a gas leak incident struck a building in Bgy Bel-Air, Makati City on Monday, May 18, authorities said. 

Responders from the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (DRRMO) conducted emergency response operations at the scene. 

According to DRRMO personnel, six individuals were classified under “red tag” or severe condition and were immediately brought to different hospitals for treatment. 

Ten individuals were classified under “green tag” or fit to go, while nine others were placed under observation under the “yellow tag” category, the report read. 

Makati City Fire Marshal F/Supt Mariano Taguiang said gas leak detection operations continued for several hours to ensure public safety. 

At around 6:55 p.m., authorities officially declared the area cleared from the gas leak. 

The incident command post was later demobilized, while police personnel remained on standby for monitoring operations. | via @jeffcaparas

(📸 BFP Makati Fire Station)
